summary: kind=schedulable, feature: the hourly Tier 2 notification-channel health check. Emitted five classes and five .cls-meta.xml siblings at apiVersion 67.0 under artefacts/M1-S04/classes/ - a thin Tier2ChannelHealthSchedulable holding the hourly CRON literal '0 0 * * * ?' whose execute() only enqueues, a Tier2ChannelHealthQueueable carrying three aggregate COUNT() queries and both Q24 thresholds, a nine-method Tier2ChannelHealthTest, plus verbatim copies of templates/apex/ApplicationLogger.cls and templates/apex/tests/TestDataFactory.cls required by the Step 6 provenance rule. All four skill checkers exit 0. Confidence is MEDIUM, not HIGH: no compile check ran because the build is design-only, and ApplicationLogger's own two metadata prerequisites - Application_Log__c and Logger_Setting__mdt - are shipped by no step of this build, which makes the package undeployable until a human settles it.
confidence_rationale: GATES.md Gate D row 3: zero unresolved symbols but no target_org_alias, so the dry-run compile did not run at all and coverage is unmeasured - computed MEDIUM, never self-declared HIGH. Gate B resolved every symbol against a file on disk (Integration_Failure__c, Case.Tier2_Notified_At__c and Status__c against artefacts/M1-S01; ApplicationLogger and TestDataFactory against templates/apex). Application_Log__c and Logger_Setting__mdt resolve to template files too, which is why this is a deploy-order finding rather than a Gate B refusal.

findings.title: ApplicationLogger is wired per include_logger:true, but Application_Log__c and Logger_Setting__mdt are shipped by no step of this build
findings.detail: Step input include_logger:true means every class wires through templates/apex/ApplicationLogger.cls (apex-builder Inputs table). That class writes Application_Log__c rows and reads Logger_Setting__mdt.getInstance('Default'). skills/apex/error-handling-framework/references/code-examples.md section 9 rows 1-3 make both hard compile prerequisites of shipping ApplicationLogger. Clarification Q16 answered 'We have no existing Apex log object in the org', and M1-S01's object model ships Integration_Failure__c, Case.Tier2_Notified_At__c and Tier2_Escalation__e only. apex-builder emits .cls/.trigger files only and cannot ship the object or the CMDT, and M1-S01 is already documented. The step's classes therefore do not compile in the target org as it stands.
findings.recommendation: A human chooses at the M1 gate: (a) add an object-model step owned by metadata-builder shipping templates/apex/custom_objects/Application_Log__c plus its eight fields and templates/apex/cmdt/Logger_Setting__mdt with a Default record, which M1-S03 and M1-S04 then depend on; or (b) amend-step this step's inputs.include_logger to false and re-run it, accepting that a suppressed alert leaves no queryable record. Nothing in this run guesses between them.

findings.title: The plan's outputs[] does not declare the two template copies its own templates[] requires
findings.detail: templates[] cites templates/apex/ApplicationLogger.cls and templates/apex/tests/TestDataFactory.cls; outputs[] declares six paths, none of them those copies or their meta XML. Step 6's provenance rule forces them into the package, so five files (four class/meta files plus deploy-order.md) land as undeclared artefacts that check-outputs never confirms.
findings.recommendation: The writer is build_plan.py amend-step, and it is refused once a step has left pending - so this is a note for whoever re-plans, not a fix this run can apply. standards/build-orchestration.md section 4's Apex row note names the structural remedy: a dedicated Apex foundations step, since M1-S03 and M1-S04 share both dependencies.

findings.title: The Support Engineering recipient address is bound by no answer, so alertRecipients ships empty with a // UNKNOWN: marker
findings.detail: Q24 names the team, not an address, and the step input says the address comes from the deploy-order note rather than being hardcoded per environment. A Custom Metadata Type or Custom Label is the right home; no step in this build ships either, and a reference to a Custom Label that does not exist is a compile error. sendAlert logs 'Channel health alert NOT sent' and returns when the list is empty, so an unconfigured job is loud rather than silently mailing nowhere.
findings.recommendation: Set the list at release, or add the configuration metadata in the same change as AB-01 fix (a).

findings.title: The scheduling user's Case record visibility is not guaranteed, and an under-count raises a false dead-channel alert
findings.detail: Tier2_Webhook_Admin grants viewAllRecords on Integration_Failure__c, so both failure counts are complete for any assignee. It carries no objectPermissions row for Case (assumption A14), so the successesLastDay query returns only Cases the scheduling user can see under the org's Case sharing model. If that user cannot see other people's Cases, successesLastDay reads 0 and rule 2 fires on a healthy channel.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the scheduling user's Case access at the M1 gate. No answer names a Case OWD, so nothing was assumed here.

findings.title: While the channel is dark the job emails Support Engineering every hour for up to 24 hours
findings.detail: Q24 asked for the alert and said nothing about repetition, and no answer names an acknowledgement mechanism, so no suppression was invented. At most 24 of the org's 5,000 daily external emails, which counts recipients rather than calls.
findings.recommendation: If alert fatigue matters, the cheapest suppression is a high-water-mark field on a configuration record - which needs metadata this build does not ship. Decide at the M1 gate.

process_observations.observation: M1-S01 shipped Case.Tier2_Notified_At__c with a description naming this health check as a consumer, so the field's purpose was verifiable from the artefact rather than inferred from the plan.
M1-S02's permission set grants viewAllRecords on Integration_Failure__c, which is what makes the two failure counts trustworthy for any assignee under the Private OWD decision D12 set.

Noticed that include_logger:true pulls in two metadata components no step of this build ships, so the emitted package cannot compile in the target org until the object model gains Application_Log__c and Logger_Setting__mdt.

Noticed that M1-S03 cites the same two template classes and declares no output for either, so both Apex steps carry the same undeclared-copy problem and the plan has no Apex foundations step to hold them.

Noticed that check_apex_scheduled_jobs.py blanks line comments before string literals, so a '//' inside an Apex string literal mis-lexes the remainder of the file; the seeded endpoint value in the test drops its scheme to stay out of that path.

The step input says execute() does nothing but enqueue while also setting include_logger:true; one ApplicationLogger.info plus flush was kept in execute() and the tension is recorded so a strict reader can delete those two lines.

No cited skill states whether WITH USER_MODE may be appended to an aggregate COUNT() query, so the clause was omitted on the authority of the step input and the API 67.0 default-user-mode row rather than guessed either way.
A security pass over the emitted classes would independently confirm the user-mode reading of the three aggregate queries against the assignee set decision D14 names.
process_observations.followup_reason: because the FLS and sharing reading of three unqualified 67.0 queries is exactly what that agent re-derives from the code rather than from the plan's claim about it.

process_observations.observation: The Apex foundations gap - two steps sharing two template classes with no step owning them - is a change-planning question rather than a coding one.
process_observations.followup_reason: because adding Application_Log__c and Logger_Setting__mdt to a documented milestone touches deploy order for M1-S03, M1-S04 and M1-S05 at once.
